newsitem.title: CHINA: HK's Tung to consult public on poll arrangements.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tung to consult public on poll arrangements.

text.p: Hong Kong's new leader Tung Chee-hwa launched a pulse-taking exercise on Wednesday to gather public views on how the territory should hold its first elections since becoming part of China.
The territory's 6.4 million people have until July 31 to make their views known on the first Legislative Council polls, which are due to be held in the second quarter next year.
Critics charged the nine-day exercise was inadequate as public consultations usually last for weeks.
"(The government) can justify it does the task ... I don't think it is a good attitude," said Frederick Fung, chairman of a centrist party, the Association for Democracy and People's Livelihood.
The public will also have no chance to have a say on Tung's plan to adopt proportional representation in the 20 geographical constituencies, abolishing the British-style electoral set-up.
Analysts and Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp have said the new voting system would slash the chances of democrats in the Legislative Council polls.
Beijing disbanded the elected 60-seat legislature and replaced it with an appointed chamber when it took back Hong Kong from Britain on July 1.
Western leaders and Hong Kong's democracy advocates have urged China to hold an election as soon as possible.

The public consultation will deal with the question of which business and professional groups should share the 30 "functional constituency" seats. It will also ask for input on the composition of the 800-strong Election Committee, which will name 10 people to the legislature.
